subject: System Design
title: How DNS Resolution Works
description: A 60-second lesson on How DNS Resolution Works.

hook.text: You type google.com. But your browser needs an IP address. DNS translates the name in milliseconds.

buildup.text: Your browser asks a recursive resolver, which queries root servers, TLD servers, and authoritative servers.

discovery.text: Root servers direct to .com servers. The .com servers direct to Google's nameservers. They return the IP.

twist.text: This happens for every new domain you visit. DNS caching at each level prevents repeating the full lookup.

climax.text: DNS is the internet's phone book. Without it, you'd need to memorize IP addresses for every website.

punchline.text: DNS turns names into IP addresses in milliseconds.

quiz.question: What is the role of DNS?
options: Translating domain names into IP addresses
